Here,
$$q_1 = 1\text{ C}$$
$$q_2 = -1\text{ C}$$
$$r = 10\text{ cm} = 0.10\text{ m}$$
$$k = 9 \times 10^9\text{ Nm}^2/\text{C}^2$$

So,
$$F = \frac{9 \times 10^9 \times 1 \times (-1)}{(0.10)^2}\text{ N} = -9 \times 10^{11}\text{ N}$$

Question: Two charges of $+5\text{ C}$ and $+3\text{ C}$ are placed at a distance of $1\text{ m}$. Now a third charge $+q$ is placed in between them, where will it not feel any force. (Figure 10.10 b).

Answer: The $+5\text{ C}$ charge will repel $+q$ charge towards the right and the $+3\text{ C}$ charge repel towards the left. When two charges will repel by equal force, $+q$ charge will not feel any force.

So,
$$k\frac{(+5)q}{x^2} = k\frac{(+3)q}{(1 - x)^2}$$
$$5(1 - x)^2 = 3x^2$$
$$2x^2 - 10x + 5 = 0$$
$$x = \frac{10 \pm \sqrt{100 - 40}}{4}$$
$$x = 4.435\text{ or }0.565$$

As the value of $x$ will be between $0$ and $1$, so the value of $x$ must be $0.565$.
(Can you try what it would be if the value of $x$ was $4.435$?)
